newsitem.title: USA: Trial for former banker Bynum will start Monday.
newsitem.headline: Trial for former banker Bynum will start Monday.

text.p: The perjury trial of former Arkansas investment banker Preston Bynum will begin on Monday as scheduled, prosecutors and Bynum's attorney said Thursday.
A court clerk had mistakenly told Reuters that the trial was postponed indefinitely.
Bynum's attorney, Jack Lassiter, said the confusion arose because the trial was postponed from its original date in May, when Bynum underwent open-heart surgery.
"It was continued then. My client was a pretty sick guy and had some open heart surgery," Lassiter said.
Bynum has recovered but the new trial date was not entered in all of the court records.
Gayle Kinsley, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Attorney's Office, also confirmed jury selection in the case would begin Monday morning in U.S. District Court in Pensacola.

Bynum resigned from the Little Rock, Ark., firm Stephans Inc after pleading guilty in 1995 to a bribery charge. He admitted he paid Terry Busbee, a former commissioner with the Escambia County Utility Authority, $67,200 in loans and cash to steer municipal bond underwriting business to the firm.

Bynum was subsequently charged with perjury in an indictment unsealed in March. The indictment alleges he lied to a grand jury when he said that he thought the money would be used to pay a consultant. The indictment alleges Bynum knew the money was for Busbee.
